# **Preface** {#preface}

This Software Design Document (SDD) describes the architectural and detailed design of DASIGConnect, a multi-tenant social media content management system developed for the Department of Science and Technology — Accelerated Science and Technology Human Resource Development Program (DOST DASIG). The system is designed to replace ad hoc coordination between member institutions and a centralized Administrator by introducing a structured, self-service content submission and publication workflow integrated with the DASIG Facebook Page.

This document translates the functional and non-functional requirements defined in the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) into concrete design decisions: system architecture, component structure, data models, API contracts, security mechanisms, and AI integration design. Where the SRS defines *what* the system must do, this document defines *how* the system does it.

## ***Intended Audience*** {#intended-audience}

This document is intended for the development team responsible for implementing and maintaining DASIGConnect. It assumes familiarity with the SRS and working knowledge of the technologies involved, including Spring Boot, PostgreSQL with pgvector, React, the Facebook Graph API, and the Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Voyage AI APIs. It may also be referenced by technical reviewers and DASIG stakeholders evaluating design decisions during the pilot period.

## ***Relationship to Other Documents*** {#relationship-to-other-documents}

This SDD should be read in conjunction with the SRS, which remains the authoritative reference for system requirements, business rules, guard rails, and non-functional constraints. Where this document references a requirement by its identifier (e.g., GR-H1, BR-ACC-03, UC-1.3), the SRS is the source of record for that requirement's full specification. Any conflict between this document and the SRS shall be resolved in favor of the SRS unless a formal change request has been approved.

## ***Design Conventions*** {#design-conventions}

Throughout this document, the term *shall* denotes a design decision that directly implements a mandatory requirement from the SRS. The term *is* or *uses* describes an implementation choice made within the latitude allowed by the requirements. Sequence diagrams follow UML 2.x notation. All API endpoint paths are relative to the application base URL and are prefixed with `/api/v1` unless otherwise noted.

# **1\. Introduction** {#1.-introduction}

## ***1.1. Purpose*** {#1.1.-purpose}

This Software Design Description (SDD) defines the architectural and detailed design of DASIGConnect — a web-based Social Media Content Workflow and Scheduling Management System developed for the DOST Acadême–Science and Innovation Group (DASIG) under DOST Region 7\. DASIGConnect centralizes and automates the social media content coordination operations of the DASIG multi-institutional network, specifically targeting its official Facebook page.

This document translates the functional and non-functional requirements specified in the DASIGConnect Software Requirements Specification (SRS) into concrete design decisions. It covers the system architecture, user interface design, front-end component structure, back-end component design, object-oriented models, and data design for all twenty-one use cases across three development modules. It serves as the authoritative technical reference for the development team throughout the entire project lifecycle.

## ***1.2. Scope*** {#1.2.-scope}

This SDD covers the complete design of DASIGConnect across three modules:

**Module 1 — User Access & Content Creation**

* 1.1 Administrator Account Management (UC-1.1)

* 1.2 Institution Management (UC-1.2)

* 1.3 Contributor Account Management (UC-1.3)

* 1.4 Login & Session Management (UC-1.4)

* 1.5 Post Drafting & Templates (UC-1.5)

* 1.6 AI & Text Tools Integration (UC-1.6)

* 1.7 Media Attachment Rules (UC-1.7)

* 1.8 Engagement Helpers (UC-1.8)

* 1.9 Draft Submission (UC-1.9)

* 1.10 Moderator Account Management (UC-1.10)

**Module 2 — Media Library & Approval Pipeline**

* 2.1 Library Uploads & Albums (UC-2.1)

* 2.2 Semantic Search & Filtering (UC-2.2)

* 2.3 Media History Tracking (UC-2.3)

* 2.4 Admin Approval Workflow (UC-2.4)

* 2.5 Automated Watermarking (UC-2.5)

**Module 3 — Scheduling, Publishing, & Analytics**

* 3.1 Master Calendar Visibility (UC-3.1)

* 3.2 Automated Facebook Post Publishing (UC-3.2)

* 3.3 Automated Reminders & Alerts (UC-3.3)

* 3.4 Social Engagement Analytics (UC-3.4)

* 3.5 System Health Analytics (UC-3.5)

* 3.6 Audit Log Review (UC-3.6)

The system is built on a React single-page application front end, a Spring Boot REST API back end, and a PostgreSQL relational database with the pgvector extension hosted on Supabase (database only). Media files and generated derivatives are stored in Cloudflare R2 through an S3-compatible integration: the browser uploads directly to R2 using backend-issued presigned URLs, and media is read through the backend's own media proxy. Five external services are integrated: the Facebook Graph API v25.0 for automated post publishing, Page engagement retrieval, and Messenger notification delivery; the Anthropic Claude API (Claude Haiku 4.5, vision-capable) for AI caption generation, proofreading, template drafting, and image classification; the Google Gemini API for optional structured media metadata enrichment; the Voyage AI API (`voyage-4-lite` text and `voyage-multimodal-3.5` image embeddings, 1024 dimensions) for semantic media search and recommendation; and the Resend email API for notification and account-activation email delivery.

## ***1.3. Definitions and Acronyms*** {#1.3.-definitions-and-acronyms}

* **Admin Owner** — A governance flag (`users.is_admin`) held by exactly one active Administrator. It is not a separate role. It is required for actions targeting existing Administrator accounts, account erasure, Admin Owner transfer, and connecting a different Facebook Page.

* **ERD** — Entity-Relationship Diagram — a visual representation of the database schema and table relationships.

* **Fast-Track (Live Event)** — A submission mode that skips scheduled-slot selection and publishes asynchronously immediately after approval.

* **Guard Rails** — Network-wide scheduling rules (conflict buffer, minimum lead time, posting window, maximum horizon, per-institution quota, daily cap — defaults ±30 min, 2 h, 8:00 AM–8:00 PM, 30 days, 3, 6), all Administrator-configurable and enforced when the runtime switch `page_settings.guardrails_enforced` is on.

* **JPA** — Java Persistence API — the Java standard specification for object-relational mapping; implemented by Hibernate in Spring Data JPA.

* **JWT** — JSON Web Token — a compact, URL-safe token format used for stateless authentication; implemented using the jjwt library in Spring Boot.

* **ORM** — Object-Relational Mapper — an abstraction layer between application code and the database; DASIGConnect uses Spring Data JPA with Hibernate.

* **pgvector** — A PostgreSQL extension enabling `VECTOR(1024)` column storage and cosine similarity nearest-neighbor search for Voyage AI embeddings.

* **Presigned URL** — A short-lived, signed R2 URL issued by the backend that lets the browser `PUT` file bytes directly to object storage without the backend receiving the file.

* **R2** — Cloudflare R2, the S3-compatible object storage service used for media files and generated watermark derivatives.

* **RBAC** — Role-Based Access Control — a security model in which access is granted based on the user's assigned role (Contributor, Moderator, or Administrator, with a single Administrator additionally holding the Admin Owner flag).

* **REST** — Representational State Transfer — the architectural style used for the Spring Boot back-end API.

* **RLS** — Row-Level Security — a PostgreSQL feature enforcing per-institution data isolation at the database level.

* **SDD** — Software Design Description: this document.

* **Spring Boot** — An open-source Java-based framework used to build the DASIGConnect REST API back end, providing auto-configuration, embedded server, and production-ready features.

* **Spring Data JPA** — A Spring Boot module providing repository abstractions (JpaRepository) over JPA/Hibernate, used as the primary data access layer throughout DASIGConnect.

* **Spring Security** — A Spring Boot module providing authentication, JWT verification, and role-based access control through `@PreAuthorize` method security.

* **SRS** — Software Requirements Specification — the companion requirements document for DASIGConnect.

* **SSE** — Server-Sent Events — an HTTP-based protocol used by DASIGConnect for real-time server-to-client push notifications.

* **UUID** — Universally Unique Identifier — used as primary keys throughout the data model.

# **2\. Architectural Design** {#2.-architectural-design}

DASIGConnect follows a three-tier client-server architecture designed around a single guiding principle: routine, high-volume work is handled by Contributors within system-enforced rules and centralized Moderator/Administrator review, while the Administrator's exception-handling role is reserved for situations where human judgment provides genuine value beyond routine review. The architecture enforces this principle through a layered design where each tier has a clearly bounded responsibility.

## ***Architectural Overview*** {#architectural-overview}

### ***Presentation Tier*** {#presentation-tier}

The front end is a React 19 \+ TypeScript single-page application built with Vite and served via Vercel's global CDN. Users access DASIGConnect through a standard web browser with no additional installations required. The SPA handles all routing, component rendering, and state management client-side, communicating with the back end exclusively through RESTful API calls over HTTPS and persistent SSE connections for real-time notifications. Media bytes are uploaded directly to Cloudflare R2 through backend-issued presigned URLs.

| Technology | Role |
| ----- | ----- |
| React 19 \+ TypeScript (Vite) | SPA framework — functional components, hooks, Context API |
| React Router v7 | Client-side routing; access grouped by layout-route gates (`RequireSignedIn`, `RequireReviewer`, `RequireAdmin`) |
| Tailwind CSS v4 \+ shadcn/ui \+ Radix UI | Utility-first styling and accessible UI primitives |
| Axios | HTTP client; Authorization header managed by `setAuthToken`; response interceptor normalizes the `{error: {code, message}}` envelope and triggers the session-expired modal on 401 |
| TanStack Query (React Query) | Server-state caching, background refetch, and request de-duplication |
| FullCalendar.js | Master Calendar — week/month views, drag-and-drop rescheduling, color-coded state cards |
| React Context \+ custom hooks | Authentication/session state (`useAuthSession`, `useSessionCountdown`, `useLoginLockout`) and toast notifications |
| EventSource (SSE) | Real-time in-app notifications and read-state sync |

### ***Application Tier*** {#application-tier}

The back end is a Spring Boot 4 (Java 21\) REST API server deployed on Railway. It handles all business logic, state machine enforcement, guard rail validation, external API orchestration, tenant isolation, and background job scheduling. The API is stateless — session state is carried in the JWT issued at login, while revocation is persisted in the database.

| Technology | Role |
| ----- | ----- |
| Spring Boot 4 (Spring Web MVC) | REST API framework — auto-configuration, embedded Tomcat server |
| Spring Security | JWT authentication filter (`JwtAuthenticationFilter`), RBAC via `@PreAuthorize`, tenant scope resolution (`TenantScopeService`) |
| Spring Data JPA \+ Hibernate | ORM layer — JpaRepository interfaces, JPQL queries, native SQL for pgvector and atomic conditional updates |
| Flyway | Versioned schema migrations (`db/migration`, V1–V122); Hibernate DDL generation is not used |
| HikariCP | JDBC connection pool, capped at 5 connections for the Supabase Session Pooler |
| jjwt | JWT generation, signing (HS256), and verification |
| Java `HttpClient` (java.net.http) | Synchronous HTTP client for the Facebook Graph API, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Voyage AI, and Resend |
| AWS SDK for Java v2 (S3) | S3-compatible client for Cloudflare R2 (presigned PUT, download, delete, bucket scan) |
| Spring `@Scheduled` | Background cron and fixed-delay jobs (publishing, stale detection, token health, embedding reconciliation, retention, and others — see Background Processing) |
| Spring `@Cacheable` | In-memory caching for the analytics summary (60-second TTL) |
| Spring Application Events | Decoupled notification dispatch, Fast-Track publishing (`@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)`), and watermark failure alerts |
| In-memory rate limiters | Per-user hourly limits for AI caption (30/h), proofreading (30/h), and top-post template generation (10/h); account lockout for login |

### ***Data Tier*** {#data-tier}

The database is PostgreSQL hosted on Supabase, with Row-Level Security (RLS) policies enforcing per-institution data isolation at the database level. The pgvector extension enables `VECTOR(1024)` storage and cosine similarity nearest-neighbor search for the Voyage AI embeddings powering semantic search, media recommendation, and album matching. Media files are stored in Cloudflare R2 and served through the backend media proxy.

| Technology | Role |
| ----- | ----- |
| PostgreSQL (Supabase) | Primary relational database — users, institutions, submissions, media metadata, notifications, analytics caches, and audit data |
| pgvector | `VECTOR(1024)` columns in `media_asset_embeddings` (and legacy `media_assets.embedding`) and the `<=>` cosine distance operator |
| Row-Level Security (RLS) | Database-level tenant isolation and append-only enforcement for `audit_log` |
| GiST exclusion constraint | Network-wide ±30-minute slot conflict protection on `slot_reservations` (GR-H1), exempting only explicit Administrator overrides |
| Cloudflare R2 | Object storage for uploaded media, institution logos, and transient watermarked derivatives (`generated/watermarked/`) |
| Backend media proxy | `GET /api/v1/media-files/{objectPath}` (`MediaProxyController`) — stable, unauthenticated read URL stored in `media_assets.storage_url` |

### ***External Service Integrations*** {#external-service-integrations}

| Service | Provider | Purpose |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Facebook Graph API v25.0 | Meta | Automated post publishing (two-step photo method \+ single-call video method), Page token validation and OAuth re-authorization, post/Page engagement retrieval, Messenger notification delivery and link-code webhook |
| Anthropic Claude API (Claude Haiku 4.5, vision) | Anthropic | AI caption generation (UC-1.6), writing check/proofreading (UC-1.6, UC-2.4), image classification and description (UC-2.1), top-post template drafting (UC-1.5 A11), content idea suggestions (UC-3.3) |
| Google Gemini API (gemini-3.8-flash, configurable) | Google | Image classification (UC-2.1) into one of 14 categories plus an asset type, factual description, and up to 30 tags, with structured enrichment (scenes, objects, activities, OCR text, event hypotheses) used to improve search and recommendation |
| Voyage AI API (`voyage-4-lite`, `voyage-multimodal-3.5`) | Voyage AI | 1024-dimension semantic (text) and image embeddings for semantic search (UC-2.2), AI-Suggested Media and Album Auto-Match (UC-1.7) |
| Resend API | Resend | Transactional email — invitations, password reset, notification emails (single attempt per email; no automatic retry) |
| Cloudflare R2 | Cloudflare | S3-compatible media object storage |

### ***Background Processing*** {#background-processing}

| Job | Schedule | Purpose |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| PublishingSchedulerJob | Every minute | Claims and publishes due `scheduled` / `direct_post_scheduled` submissions within a 5-minute lookback (UC-3.2) |
| StaleSubmissionDetectorJob | Every 5 minutes | Missed scheduled post → `publish_failed`; never-reviewed post past its slot → `missed_review` (slot released); recovers stuck `publishing` rows including Fast-Track (GR-T9) |
| TokenPublishingEscalationJob | Every 5 minutes | Retries token-blocked submissions once a usable token exists; escalates at 24h and fails at 48h (UC-3.2 A3) |
| ReviewLockCleanupJob | Every minute | Expires 15-minute review locks and reverts `in_review` → `pending` (UC-2.4 A4) |
| ValidationDeadlineNotificationJob | Every 5 minutes | Reviewer deadline alerts for submissions nearing their slot; the GR-T1 priority flag itself is computed when the queue is read |
| AbandonmentDetectorJob | Every 5 minutes | Clears manual-publish sessions open longer than 2 hours (UC-2.4 A8) |
| TokenHealthCheckJob | Daily | Validates the active Facebook Page token; expiry and invalid-token alerts (GR-T3, GR-T4) |
| EmbeddingReconciliationJob | Every 30 seconds (app.media-processing.reconcile-delay-ms) | Re-queues image assets missing current embeddings in bounded batches; jobs that exhaust 5 attempts are dead-lettered and the asset is marked FAILED (GR-T7) |
| MediaProcessingWorker | Polls every second | Leases and runs `media_processing_jobs` (classification, enrichment, embeddings, submission media context) with retry and dead-letter handling |
| SocialEngagementSyncJob | Every 15 minutes | Refreshes cached Facebook post engagement (`submission_engagement_metrics`) (UC-3.4) |
| InvitationExpiryJob | Hourly | Transitions expired `pending`/`pending_email_undelivered` accounts to `expired` (GR-T8) |
| StaleDraftSlotReleaseJob | Daily 02:00 UTC | Releases slots held by drafts inactive for 7 days (GR-T2) |
| MediaAssetRetentionPurgeJob | Daily 02:30 UTC | Purges soft-deleted media after the 30-day retention window |
| GeneratedWatermarkPurgeJob | Daily 02:45 UTC | Deletes watermarked derivatives older than 3 days (UC-2.5) |
| EmptyScheduleWarningJob | Weekly (Mon) | Empty-schedule warning with AI content-idea suggestions (T-07) |
| EmbeddingFailureDigestJob | Weekly (Mon) | Embedding failure digest to Administrators (T-12) |
| AuditLogRetentionJob | Daily 03:45 UTC | Retention purge of aged audit entries |
| ScheduledJobRunRetentionJob | Daily 03:15 UTC | Prunes old `scheduled_job_runs` history |
| RevokedTokenCleanupJob | Hourly | Deletes expired `revoked_tokens` rows |

Every tracked job records its runs in `scheduled_job_runs`, which feeds System Health (UC-3.5). Administrators may re-run any tracked job on demand through `ManualJobRunner`. Sixteen jobs are tracked; AuditLogRetentionJob, RevokedTokenCleanupJob, and the MediaProcessingWorker are scheduled but not tracked on System Health.

### ***Security Architecture Overview*** {#security-architecture-overview}

Tenant isolation is enforced through four complementary layers ensuring no cross-institution data leakage:

1. **JWT-Based Tenant Binding** — `institution_id` is embedded as a verified claim in every Contributor token; Moderator and Administrator tokens carry no `institution_id` (network-wide). The claim is verified and attached to the request context by `JwtAuthenticationFilter` before any controller logic executes. Every token also carries `session_version`; revoked or outdated tokens are rejected inside `JWTService.extractClaims` (backed by `revoked_tokens` and `users.session_version`).

2. **Application Query Filters** — `TenantScopeService` resolves the caller's scope; every institution-scoped query applies the `institution_id` filter for Contributors.

3. **PostgreSQL RLS** — Database-level policies return zero rows for cross-institution queries and make `audit_log` insert-only.

4. **Server-Derived Identity** — `institution_id` on new records is always set from the authenticated session (or, for Moderators/Administrators, from the validated "Posting As" selection), never trusted from the request body.

Additional controls: BCrypt password hashing, a 12-character password policy, 5-attempt/15-minute account lockout, AES-256-GCM encryption of Facebook Page tokens (`TokenEncryptionService`), HMAC-signed stateless OAuth `state`, formula-injection-safe CSV exports, and secrets supplied only through Railway environment variables.

# **3\. Detailed Design** {#3.-detailed-design}

## ***1\. Module 1*** {#1.-module-1}

Module 1 establishes the system foundation: secure user authentication with role-based routing, institution workspace provisioning, invitation-based onboarding for all three roles, and the three-step post composer with integrated AI caption, writing-check, template, media, and scheduling tools.

### ***1.1. Administrator Account Management*** {#1.1.-administrator-account-management}

#### ***1.1.1. User Interface Design***

**Admin Management Screen (`/admin/admin-management`)**

A table listing all Administrator accounts with name, email, status badge (PENDING, PENDING\_EMAIL\_UNDELIVERED, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, EXPIRED, CANCELLED), and an "Admin Owner" tag on the single owner account. An "Invite Administrator" action is available to any Administrator while the combined Admin cap (active Admins \+ outstanding Admin invitations \+ pending promotions ≤ 3\) is not reached. Deactivate, Reactivate, Delete, Erase, Demote, and Transfer Admin Owner actions are rendered only for the Admin Owner; peer Administrators see them disabled. Pending Administrator invitations appear in a separate card with Resend and Cancel actions.

**Invite Administrator Dialog**

An email chip input with a Send Invitation button. On success the dialog closes with a toast and the account appears with PENDING status. A cap violation returns an inline error directing the actor to remove or transfer an existing Administrator first.

**Change Role / Promote Dialog**

Opened from User Management on an ACTIVE Moderator or Contributor. Proposing a promotion to Administrator creates a pending request; the target's role does not change until they confirm. Demotion of an Administrator (Admin Owner only) is immediate; demotion to Contributor requires selecting an active institution.

**Promotion and Owner-Transfer Confirmation Prompts**

Shown to the target user on their next session when a pending promotion (72-hour expiry) or Admin Owner transfer (24-hour expiry) exists, with Confirm and Decline actions.

**Invitation Accept Page (`/invite?token=…`)**

A public route shared by all invitation flows. Validates the token, then displays a password setup form (New Password, Confirm Password) with live per-rule validation of the 12-character password policy. Submit stays disabled until all rules pass.

#### ***1.1.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**AdministratorManagementScreen**

* Lists Administrators via `GET /users/admins` and pending Admin invitations via `GET /invitations/pending/admins`. Renders owner-only actions from `User.adminOwner` in the authenticated profile (`GET /me`).

* React functional component / Admin route (`RequireAdmin`)

  **InvitationComposer / EmailChipsInput**

* Controlled form submitting `POST /invitations` with `role = admin` and no institution. Shows inline cap and conflict errors.

* React functional component

  **ChangeRoleModal / ConfirmDialog**

* Submits `PATCH /users/{id}/role` (propose promotion or demote), `PATCH /users/{id}/status` (deactivate/reactivate), `DELETE /users/{id}` (delete), `POST /users/{id}/erase`, `POST /users/{id}/admin-transfer`, and `DELETE /users/{id}/promotion` (cancel proposal).

* React functional components

  **Promotion / Transfer Confirmation**

* Calls `POST /users/promotion/confirm`, `POST /users/promotion/decline`, and `POST /users/admin-transfer/confirm`.

* React functional component rendered in the authenticated shell

  **InviteScreen**

* Public route validating via `GET /invitations/validate?token=…` and activating via `POST /invitations/accept`. Shared across all three roles.

* React functional component

#### ***1.1.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**InvitationController**

* `POST /invitations` (Admin/Moderator; role-gated per caller), `GET /invitations/validate`, `POST /invitations/accept`, `POST /invitations/{id}/resend`, `DELETE /invitations/{id}` (cancel), `GET /invitations/pending/admins` (Admin).

* Spring `@RestController`

  **UserController**

* `GET /users/admins`, `PATCH /users/{id}/status`, `PATCH /users/{id}/role`, `DELETE /users/{id}`, `POST /users/{id}/erase`, `POST /users/{id}/admin-transfer`, `POST /users/admin-transfer/confirm`, `POST /users/promotion/confirm|decline`, `DELETE /users/{id}/promotion`.

* Spring `@RestController`

  **InvitationService**

* Generates a 32-byte CSPRNG token (72-hour validity), stores only its SHA-256 hash, reuses PENDING / PENDING\_EMAIL\_UNDELIVERED / CANCELLED / EXPIRED account rows, rejects ACTIVE and INACTIVE targets (INACTIVE must be reactivated), supersedes older open tokens, and re-checks the Admin cap (`app.admins.max`, default 3\) at both invite and accept.

* Spring `@Service`

  **UserService**

* Implements deactivate/reactivate (cap-checked, no exclusions), footprint-aware delete (`USER_REMOVED` anonymized row vs. hard delete), erase (`USER_ANONYMIZED`), propose/confirm/decline/cancel promotion through one unified pending-promotion record (`pending_promotion_role` \= admin or moderator; Admin cap re-checked at confirm via `AdminCapPolicy`; sessions revoked), demotion, and Admin Owner transfer (to another ACTIVE Administrator only — a non-Administrator target is rejected with 400; on confirmation the flag moves and both accounts remain Administrators). Self-targeting is rejected for every action. Owner-only checks use `JwtUserDetails.adminOwner().` 

* Spring `@Service`

  **JWTService**

* Account-wide session revocation by incrementing `users.session_version` on deactivate, role change, and promotion confirmation.

* Spring `@Service`

  **AuditLogService / EmailService / NotificationService**

* Records `INVITATION_ACCEPTED`, `USER_STATUS_UPDATED`, `USER_ROLE_CHANGED`, `USER_REMOVED`, `USER_ANONYMIZED`, `ADMIN_TRANSFER_REQUESTED`, `ADMIN_TRANSFER_CONFIRMED`, and `ADMIN_PROMOTION_*` events; dispatches activation email via Resend; notifies promotion targets and proposers.

* Spring `@Service`

  **UserRepository / InvitationTokenRepository**

* Spring `@Repository` extending `JpaRepository<User, UUID>` / `JpaRepository<InvitationToken, UUID>`

	`email                        	VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,`

	`first_name                   	VARCHAR(100),`  
	`last_name                    	VARCHAR(100),`  
	`display_name                 	VARCHAR(150),`  
	`role                         	VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL`  
                                 	`CHECK (role IN ('contributor', 'moderator', 'admin')),`  
	`account_state                	VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'`  
                                 	`CHECK (account_state IN ('pending', 'pending_email_undelivered',`  
                                            `'active', 'expired', 'inactive', 'cancelled')),`  
	`is_admin                     	BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, 	-- Admin Owner flag`  
	`session_version              	BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,      	-- account-wide revocation`  
    `super_admin_transfer_requested_by UUID REFERENCES users(id),                          	-- pending Admin Owner transfer`  
    `super_admin_transfer_expires_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,`  
	`pending_promotion_role       	VARCHAR(20)                     	-- 'admin' | 'moderator' (V118/V119)`  
                                 	`CHECK (pending_promotion_role IN ('admin', 'moderator')),`  
	`pending_promotion_requested_by   UUID REFERENCES users(id),      	-- proposing Administrator`  
	`pending_promotion_expires_at 	TIMESTAMPTZ,                    	-- 72-hour confirmation window`  
	`invited_by_user_id           	UUID REFERENCES users(id),`  
	`notify_in_app                	BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,`  
	`notify_email                 	BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,`  
	`tours_enabled                	BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,`  
	`tour_seen_screens            	JSONB,`  
	`avatar_data                  	BYTEA,`  
    `avatar_content_type          	VARCHAR(40),`  
	`avatar_updated_at            	TIMESTAMPTZ,`  
	`purged_at                    	TIMESTAMPTZ,                    	-- anonymization marker`  
	`purged_by_user_id            	UUID REFERENCES users(id),`  
	`created_at                   	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),`  
	`updated_at                   	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`  
`);`  
   
`-- Exactly one active Admin Owner at a time (V79)`  
`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_users_single_active_admin_owner ON users ((role))`  
	`WHERE role = 'admin' AND account_state = 'active' AND is_admin = TRUE;   -- exactly one active Admin Owner`  
   
`-- Invitation tokens (one-time activation links, all roles)`  
`CREATE TABLE invitation_tokens (`  
	`id             	UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),`  
	`token_hash     	VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,          	-- SHA-256 of raw CSPRNG token`  
	`recipient_email	VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,`  
	`assigned_role  	VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL`  
                       `CHECK (assigned_role IN ('contributor', 'moderator', 'admin')),`  
	`institution_id 	UUID REFERENCES institutions(id),  -- required only for contributor`  
	`created_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),     	-- scopes Moderator invitation management`  
	`expires_at     	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,          	-- 72 hours from generation`  
	`used_at        	TIMESTAMPTZ,`  
	`created_at     	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`  
`);`

`);`

### ***1.2. Institution Management*** {#1.2.-institution-management}

#### ***1.2.1. User Interface Design***

**Institution Management Screen (`/institution-management`)**

A table of registered institutions with Name, Code, Status badge (Active / Inactive), logo, and Contributor count, plus summary counts by status. Administrators see a "Register Institution" button and per-row actions (Edit, Upload Logo, Deactivate/Reactivate, Delete, Reassign Users). Moderators see the same list in read-only form with no action controls. The protected default institution "DASIG Central Visayas" shows Deactivate and Delete disabled with an explanatory tooltip.

**Register / Edit Institution Modal**

Fields: Institution Name, Institution Code (unique), and Email Domain. Inline errors are shown for a duplicate code or email domain when registering, and for a name or email domain already used by another institution when editing.

**Deactivate Confirmation**

Blocked while Contributors remain assigned or invitations to the institution are still pending; the dialog directs the Administrator to reassign the Contributors (or resolve the invitations) first.

**Permanent Delete Confirmation**

Requires typing the institution's code. Blocked for the protected institution, any institution with PENDING/PENDING\_EMAIL\_UNDELIVERED/ACTIVE Contributors, any submission history, or any non-deleted media.

**Reassign User**

From User Management, an Administrator moves a Contributor to another ACTIVE institution; historical submissions stay attributed to the original institution.

#### ***1.2.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**InstitutionManagementScreen**

* Fetches `GET /institutions` and `GET /institutions/summary-counts`; hosts create/edit/deactivate/reactivate/delete dialogs. Role-aware rendering (Admin vs. Moderator read-only).

* React functional component / Reviewer route (`RequireReviewer`)

  **Institution Logo Upload**

* `PUT /institutions/{id}/logo` (multipart); logos are served by `GET /institutions/{id}/logo`.

* React functional component

  **Reassign Action (User Management)**

* `PATCH /users/{id}/institution`.

* React functional component

#### ***1.2.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**InstitutionController**

* `POST /institutions` (Admin), `GET /institutions`, `GET /institutions/{id}`, `GET /institutions/summary-counts`, `GET /institutions/public` (unauthenticated list used by public pages), `PUT /institutions/{id}` (Admin), `PATCH /institutions/{id}/deactivate|reactivate` (Admin), `DELETE /institutions/{id}` (Admin, code confirmation), `PUT/GET /institutions/{id}/logo`, `PATCH /institutions/{id}/ai-media-hybrid-ranking` (Admin). Class-level `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('ADMIN','MODERATOR')")`; write endpoints are Admin-only.

* Spring `@RestController`

  **InstitutionService**

* Validates uniqueness of code and email domain on create, and of name and email domain on edit; enforces protected-institution rules; blocks deactivation while Contributors are assigned or invitations to the institution are pending; performs eligibility-checked permanent deletion (cleans tokens, reservations, page settings, watermark configurations, soft-deleted media and albums, then best-effort R2 purge after commit) and writes `INSTITUTION_DELETED`.

* Spring `@Service`

  **WorkspaceProvisionerService**

* Provisions the institution workspace (default page settings and media library scoping) on creation; RLS policies are defined once in Flyway migrations and key off `institution_id`.

* Spring `@Service`

  **UserService**

* Reassigns a Contributor's `institution_id` to an ACTIVE target institution.

* Spring `@Service`

  **InstitutionRepository / AuditLogService**

* Spring `@Repository` extending `JpaRepository<Institution, UUID>`; audit entries for create, edit, deactivate, reactivate, delete, and reassignment.

"Invite Contributor" opens the invitation composer, where the actor selects an ACTIVE target institution and enters one or more emails. Administrators see Deactivate/Reactivate/Delete/Erase/Change Role actions; Moderators see only Resend, Cancel, and Delete on invitations they personally sent.

**Reissue Invitation Confirmation**

A confirmation dialog for EXPIRED, CANCELLED, PENDING, or PENDING\_EMAIL\_UNDELIVERED accounts that issues a fresh 72-hour token and invalidates the previous one.

**Invitation Accept Page (`/invite?token=…`)** — shared with UC-1.1.

#### ***1.3.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**UserInvitationsScreen / UserManagementScreen**

  **InvitationComposer**

**InvitationController** — shared with UC-1.1; Moderator access to resend/cancel/delete is restricted in `InvitationService` to tokens whose `created_by_user_id` is the caller.

**UserController**

* Spring `@RestController`

  **InvitationService**

* Rejects invitations to INACTIVE institutions (BR-ACC-01), rejects re-invitation of ACTIVE or INACTIVE accounts, binds the token to the institution (a mismatched token returns a generic invalid-token error).

  **AuditLogService / EmailService** — as in UC-1.1.

### ***1.4. Login & Session Management*** {#1.4.-login-&-session-management}

#### ***1.4.1. User Interface Design***

**Login Page (`/login`)**

A centered card with email, password (show/hide toggle), and a Log In button. Invalid credentials show a generic error. After 5 failed attempts the form is replaced by a lockout banner with the remaining duration (15 minutes). A "Forgot password?" link sits below the form. PENDING, EXPIRED, and INACTIVE accounts receive state-specific messages.

**Forgot / Reset Password Pages (`/forgot-password`, `/forgot-password-sent`, `/reset-password`)**

An email input with a neutral confirmation regardless of account existence; the reset page enforces the password policy with live per-rule feedback.

**Account Settings Screen (`/settings`)**

Tabs for Personal Settings (all roles: display name, avatar, password change, notification channel preferences, onboarding-guide toggle and reset, and — for Moderators and Administrators only — Facebook Messenger linking) and Page Settings (Administrators only: guard-rail enforcement switch and the guard-rail thresholds — conflict buffer, minimum and maximum lead time, posting-window hours, per-institution quota, daily cap — Facebook Page token management, Watermark Configuration, UC-2.5).

**Link Messenger (Personal Settings)**

Generates a 10-minute link code that the user sends to the DASIG Facebook Page in Messenger; the panel then shows the linked state with an Unlink action.

**Session Warning Banner**

Shown during the final five minutes of the JWT lifetime with "Stay Logged In" (opens the re-login modal) and "Dismiss" (hides the banner only).

**Session Expired Modal**

Opened at countdown zero or on a session-related 401\. The user re-enters email and password; a successful re-login issues a new JWT, reloads `/me`, clears authenticated query caches, and restarts the countdown.

#### ***1.4.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**LoginScreen / ForgotScreen / ForgotSentScreen / ResetPasswordScreen / NoAccountScreen**

* Submit `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/forgot-password`, `POST /auth/reset-password`.

* React functional components / public routes

  **useAuthSession / useLoginLockout / useSessionCountdown / usePasswordResetFlow**

* Session restore from stored token and `GET /me`, login with lockout feedback, JWT `exp` countdown, session-expired modal, invite activation, and sign-out (`POST /auth/logout`).

* React custom hooks

  **RouteGates (`RequireSignedIn`, `RequireReviewer`, `RequireAdmin`) / ProtectedRoute**

* Layout-route gates in `App.tsx`; unauthorized roles see `ForbiddenPage`.

* React functional components

  **DashboardShell (navigation)**

* Shows Admin Management, User Management, System Health, Audit Log, and Page Settings only to Administrators; Institution Management and Review Queue to Moderators and Administrators; Dashboard, Submissions, Calendar, Media Repository, Notifications, Analytics, and Settings to all roles.

* React layout component

  **AccountSettingsScreen**

* `PATCH /me/settings`, `PATCH /me/tour-preferences`, `POST /auth/change-password`, `PUT /users/{id}/avatar`, Messenger panel (`GET/POST/DELETE /integrations/messenger/connection[/link-code]`), and Page Settings (`GET/PUT /settings/page`).

* React functional component

#### ***1.4.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**AuthController**

* `POST /auth/login` (validate credentials and account state, issue an 8-hour JWT), `POST /auth/logout` (revoke this token only), `POST /auth/refresh` (authenticated; not currently called by the frontend).

* Spring `@RestController`

  **PasswordController / PasswordService / PasswordPolicy**

* `POST /auth/forgot-password` (neutral response; 1-hour single-use reset token), `POST /auth/reset-password` (increments `session_version`, invalidating all sessions), `POST /auth/change-password` (requires current password; other sessions unaffected). Policy: ≥12 characters, upper and lower case, digit, special character, no whitespace, no common fragments, no email/name.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **JWTService**

* HS256 tokens embedding user ID, role, `institution_id` (Contributors only), Admin Owner flag, and `session_version`. `extractClaims` rejects tokens present in `revoked_tokens` or older than the user's current `session_version`, so revocation survives restarts and spans instances.

* Spring `@Service`

  **JwtAuthenticationFilter / TenantScopeService**

* Authenticates each request and resolves the tenant scope used by services.

* Spring Security filter / `@Service`

  **AccountLockoutService**

* Tracks failed attempts in account\_lockouts; locks for 15 minutes after 5 failures (login returns 401 "Account temporarily locked" with the remaining time; no lockout email is sent).

* Spring `@Service`

  **MessengerConnectionController / MessengerWebhookController / MessengerConnectionService / MessengerWebhookService**

* Issues hashed 10-minute link codes; the Meta webhook (`GET/POST /integrations/messenger/webhook`) verifies a code sent to the Page and binds the sender's Page-scoped ID (`page_scoped_user_id`) to the user. Restricted to Moderators and Administrators.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **UserController**

* `GET /me`, `PATCH /me/settings`, `PATCH /me/tour-preferences`.

* Spring `@RestController`

  **PageSettingsController / GuardRailSettingsService**

* `GET/PUT /settings/page` (Admin) toggles the network-wide `guardrails_enforced` switch and sets every guard-rail threshold: conflict buffer (default 30 min), minimum lead time (2 h), maximum lead time (30 days), posting window (8–20), per-institution active quota (3), and daily volume cap (6), all read through `GuardRailSettingsService`. Page Settings changes are not written to the audit log.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **RevokedTokenCleanupJob**

* Hourly removal of expired revoked-token rows.

### ***1.5. Post Drafting & Templates*** {#1.5.-post-drafting-&-templates}

#### ***1.5.1. User Interface Design***

**Submissions List (`/submissions`)**

A server-paginated list of the actor's submissions with filter tabs: Drafts, Action Needed, Submitted, Published, Rejected, Failed, All. Each card shows the media thumbnail, event title, status badge, and last-updated time. A "New Post" button opens the composer; an optional onboarding guide explains the list.

**Composer Wizard (`/submissions/new`, `/submissions/:submissionId`)**

A three-step wizard — **Media → Post Details → Organize & Schedule** — with a step indicator, Next/Back navigation (forward gated by the step's Required items; Back always enabled), and a persistent Save as Draft button. Once a draft exists, changes autosave after a short delay. The desktop layout is two columns (form \+ Readiness panel); at ≤900 px the Readiness panel opens as a bottom sheet from a status chip (`Required: X of 7` / `Required: 7 of 7 ✓`) and the Submit/Save Draft bar is sticky, with **Submit for Approval** promoted as the primary always-visible action across all steps once all 7 required checks pass.

**Step 2 — Post Details**

"Posting As" institution selector (Moderators and Administrators; defaults to DASIG Central Visayas), Event Title, Event Date, and Caption (3,000-character limit, live counter). The caption action row contains **Suggest Caption**, **Templates**, **Fancy text**, and **Check writing**; an empty caption shows a "Need a head start?" starter. Hashtag pills insert into the caption.

**Post Templates Panel**

Opened from the Templates button (a right-hand drawer on desktop, a bottom sheet on small screens). Pinned header actions: **Generate from Top Posts** and **Save current caption**. Filters: All / Built-in / My templates. Applying a template requires at least one attached media item, replaces the caption, records the template, and clears current tags.

**Submission Gate & Post Quality Tips Panel (Readiness Checklist)**

Separates submission readiness into two distinct signals with no blended percentage: (1) a binary **Submission Gate** (`Required: 7 of 7 ✓ — Ready to submit` when complete, or `Required: X of 7` naming `Next: [Missing Item] →` with a direct jump link while incomplete), and (2) **Post Quality Tips** (`Tips: X of 5 applied`, clearly marked *Optional — never blocks submission*). Each row jumps to the relevant step/field. Required (7): title, date, caption, ≥1 media, file requirements, album, valid schedule (Standard). Optional Quality Tips (5): caption length, ≥1 hashtag, ≥1 media tag, ≥1 per-media caption, template used or skipped.

**Facebook Preview**

A persistent toggle showing an in-page Facebook-style preview of caption, media carousel, and hashtags.

**Revision Feedback**

A `needs_revision` submission reopens with reviewer remarks parsed into per-field comments (pulsing fields, "mark addressed"); a `rejected` submission shows the reason with "Edit & Resubmit".

* `GET /submissions/page` (server pagination, bucket counts), `DELETE /submissions/{id}` (draft/rejected), `POST /submissions/{id}/withdraw`.

* React functional component / Signed-in route

  **SubmissionScreen**

* Wizard state, readiness computation, autosave, dirty-state navigation guard; `GET /submissions/lookups` (institutions, guard-rail switch), `POST /submissions`, `PATCH /submissions/{id}`, `GET /submissions/{id}`.

* React functional component

  **InPageFacebookPreview / SubmissionReadOnlyView / SubmissionCardMedia**

* Preview and read-only rendering.

  **RevisionFeedbackBanner / RevisionFeedbackModal**

* Per-field reviewer remarks.

  **SpotlightTour**

* Contextual, view-only onboarding guides (submission list, composer, Save Draft); preferences persisted via `PATCH /me/tour-preferences`.

  (AI caption, Fancy Text, and Check writing components are detailed in UC-1.6; media components in UC-1.7; scheduling components in UC-1.8.)

### ***1.6. AI & Text Tools Integration*** {#1.6.-ai-&-text-tools-integration}

#### ***1.6.1. User Interface Design***

**Suggest Caption (caption action row)**

Opens a prompt dialog with an optional instruction field (280-character limit; Generate disabled past it) and a tone selector — Professional (default), Community, Energetic. Generation proceeds when there is an attached image, an existing caption, or a typed prompt. A loading state is shown during the request.

**Caption Suggestion**

Displays **one** caption in the selected tone with Insert, Regenerate, Edit, and Dismiss actions. Error states: timeout (30 s, retry available), AI unavailable (auto-recovers after \~5 s), and rate-limited (shows reset time, 30 requests/hour).

**Fancy Text Panel**

A button-opened panel (not triggered by text selection) previewing the selected caption text in Bold Serif, Italic Serif, Bold Sans-Serif, Italic Sans-Serif, and Script, plus Plain (revert). Characters without a Unicode equivalent pass through unchanged.

**Check Writing**

Disabled when the caption is empty. Returns advisory spelling, grammar, clarity, and meaning-change suggestions, each with Apply and Dismiss. Never blocks editing, saving, or submission. Also available in the reviewer edit form (UC-2.4), where it runs automatically after a caption edit and reports only problems the edit introduced.

#### ***1.6.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**AiCaptionButton / AiCaptionPromptDialog / AiCaptionSuggestion / useAiCaptionAssist**

* Submits `POST /ai/caption` (auto-saving the draft first if needed); logs outcomes best-effort to `POST /ai/caption/log` (`use`, `use_then_edited`, `dismiss`, `re_generate`, tone).

* React functional components / hook

  **FancyTextTool**

* Pure client-side Unicode mapping; respects `CAPTION_CHAR_LIMIT = 3000`.

* React functional component

  **Check Writing panel**

* `POST /ai/proofread`; applied suggestions reported to `POST /ai/proofread/applied` for adoption analytics.

* React functional component

#### ***1.6.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**CaptionController**

* `POST /ai/caption`, `POST /ai/caption/log`. 30 requests per rolling hour per user (in-memory limiter → `429` with reset headers); 280-character prompt cap (`400`).

* Spring `@RestController`

  **CaptionGenerationService**

* Builds the prompt from up to 4 images, media metadata, event title/date/institution, existing caption, instruction, and tone; detects instruction-vs-draft-refine intent; parses a requested word count (largest number, `MAX_REQUESTED_CAPTION_WORDS = 2000`) and retries up to 3 times to satisfy a requested range. Submission category is not part of the prompt.

* Spring `@Service`

  **ClaudeVisionClient**

* Java `HttpClient` wrapper for the Anthropic Messages API (`claude-haiku-4-5`); base64-encodes images, downscales images \> 5 MB in memory (70% → 50% → 35% → 25% → 15%), 30-second timeout (`504`), service errors (`503`). Legacy read fallback for old images on the private Supabase bucket via `DASIG_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.

* Spring `@Component`

  **ProofreadController / ProofreadService**

* `POST /ai/proofread` (30/hour/user, suggestions only), `POST /ai/proofread/applied`.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **AiAdoptionTrackingService / AiInteractionLogRepository**

* Persists caption and proofreading interaction events to `ai_interaction_log` for AI Feature Adoption analytics (UC-3.4).

* Spring `@Service` / `@Repository`

  (Fancy Text is a client-side transformation — no back-end component.)

### ***1.7. Media Attachment Rules*** {#1.7.-media-attachment-rules}

#### ***1.7.1. User Interface Design***

**Step 1 — Media**

Device upload (drag-and-drop or picker) and a Media Library tab. Upload cards show thumbnail, progress, and status, with Retry on network failure and a remove action. Media order can be rearranged by drag.

**Media Library Tab (composer picker)**

Reuses the library browser (UC-2.2) with search and, for Moderators/Administrators, an institution filter defaulting to the submission's institution. Each result has an Attach action.

**AI Suggestions Tab**

Enabled once event title \+ caption \+ media tags reach ≥10 characters. Shows up to 8 ranked suggestions (score ≥ 0.40) with match reasons and blue AI accents; hidden when nothing clears the floor.

**Media Caption Modal**

Per-asset caption (≤500 characters, live counter) and, for photos, a "Skip watermark for this image" checkbox. A caption indicator appears on the card.

**Album Field (Organize & Schedule step)**

Select an existing album, type a new name, or click **Auto-Match**: a confident match (≥0.55) auto-fills with a reason badge; an ambiguous result (0.32–0.55) lists up to 3 ranked candidates; otherwise a "no confident match" notice is shown. Media tags are entered alongside.

**Mixed-Media Notice**

An inline notice when images and video are mixed, explaining that automated publishing will route the post to the Failed tab for manual recovery.

#### ***1.7.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**SubmissionScreen media step**

* Requests `POST /submissions/{id}/media/upload-url` (presigned R2 PUT), uploads bytes directly to R2, then registers metadata with `POST /submissions/{id}/media`. Library picks use `POST /submissions/{id}/assets`; removal `DELETE /submissions/{id}/assets/{assetId}`; reorder `PATCH /submissions/{id}/media/order`. Client-side validation of 7 formats and 50 MB.

* React functional component

  **SimilarMediaPanel (AI Suggestions)**

* `POST /ai/submissions/{id}/suggest-media`, `POST /ai/submissions/{id}/suggest-media-status`, `GET /ai/submissions/{id}/similar-media`; logs via `POST /ai/submissions/{id}/log-interaction`.

* React functional component

  **AlbumCombobox**

* Album select/create with `POST /ai/submissions/{id}/suggest-album` and ranked `suggestions`. Shared with UC-2.1.

* React functional component

  **Media Caption Modal**

* Saves per-asset caption and `skipWatermark` with the draft.

* React modal component

#### ***1.7.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**SubmissionController (media endpoints)**

* `POST /submissions/{id}/media/upload-url`, `POST /submissions/{id}/media`, `PATCH /submissions/{id}/media/order`, `POST /submissions/{id}/assets`, `DELETE /submissions/{id}/assets/{assetId}`. Enforces the 10-asset limit (BR-SUB-02).

* Spring `@RestController`

  **MediaStorageService**

* AWS S3 SDK against R2: presigned PUT URLs, server-side validation of the declared MIME type, extension, and size (file content is not inspected for magic bytes), object download, delete, and public URL resolution via the backend proxy (`{BACKEND_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/api/v1/media-files/`), or a custom R2 domain when R2\_CUSTOM\_DOMAIN\_URL is set.

* Spring `@Service`

  **AIRecommendationController / AIRecommendationService**

* `suggestMedia`: Voyage query embedding over event context → pgvector search in the submission institution's library → re-rank by semantic, visual, recency, category, and tag signals → keep score ≥ 0.40, top 8; metadata/tag fallback when embedding retrieval fails. `suggestAlbum`: blends tag overlap with closest-asset visual similarity per root album (max score, not centroid); thresholds 0.55 / 0.32.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **MediaRetrievalEmbeddingService / SubmissionMediaContextService / MediaProcessingQueueService**

* Builds retrieval embeddings and the aggregated `submission_media_contexts` used for suggestions; queues processing jobs for new uploads.

* Spring `@Service`

  **SubmissionMediaAssetRepository**

* Junction persistence with `display_order`, `caption`, `skip_watermark`.

* Spring `@Repository`

### ***1.8. Engagement Helpers*** {#1.8.-engagement-helpers}

#### ***1.8.1. User Interface Design***

**Schedule Mode (Organize & Schedule step)**

A toggle between **Schedule** (default) and **Live Event (Fast-Track)**. Fast-Track hides all date/time and recommendation UI.

**When to Post — Recommendation Tiles**

A compact row of up to 3 calendar-style slot tiles under a "When to Post \*" heading. The source explanation sits behind an ⓘ toggle; the "why" line shows only for the selected tile; a "Top pick" badge and engagement bars appear only when real Page history (`HISTORICAL`) separates the slots. With insufficient history the panel shows "Best-practice guidance" (Tue/Wed/Thu 6 PM). If the Facebook analytics call fails, the panel is hidden and the picker remains.

**Date and Time Picker**

Selecting a tile fills the fields; manual entry is always allowed. Validation is debounced; hard guard-rail blocks show as errors, and soft warnings (three-unpublished-post institution quota, six-post daily cap) show inline beneath the fields (`.sub-inline-warning`) only when guard rails are enforced.

#### ***1.8.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**EngagementRecommendationsPanel**

* `GET /engagement-recommendations` for the selected institution; skipped for Fast-Track drafts and for Administrator composers without an institution scope.

* React functional component

  **CalendarDateField / TimePickerField**

* Date/time inputs with debounced validation via `POST /submissions/{id}/evaluate-slot` (saved draft) or `POST /guardrails/validate`.

* React functional components

#### ***1.8.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**EngagementRecommendationController / EngagementRecommendationService**

* Reads the Page's last 100 posts (reactions \+ comments \+ shares) from the Graph API, buckets by weekday and hour within 8 AM–8 PM Asia/Manila, keeps the top 5 buckets when ≥20 samples exist (else default Tue/Wed/Thu 6 PM), walks a 30-day lookahead for the first matching slots, drops hard-blocked candidates, and returns up to 3 slots with soft warnings and a score.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **GuardRailController / GuardRailService / GuardRailSettingsService**

* `POST /guardrails/validate`. Hard rules: network-wide conflict buffer (GR-H1, default ±30 min), minimum lead time (GR-H2, default 2 h), maximum horizon (GR-H3, default 30 days), and posting window (GR-H4, default 8:00 AM–8:00 PM Asia/Manila). Soft: per-institution active quota (GR-S1, default 3 scheduled-but-unpublished posts) and daily volume cap (GR-S2, default 6 per day). Every threshold is Administrator-configurable in Page Settings (V116, V121, V122) and read through `GuardRailSettingsService`. The database exclusion constraint (UC-1.8 schema) stays fixed at 30 minutes regardless of the configured buffer. When the switch is off, a Contributor's slot only needs to be in the future; a schedule change made by a Moderator or Administrator is still validated, and only an Administrator may bypass a hard block with a reason (audited `SCHEDULE_GUARDRAIL_OVERRIDE`). Returns a structured `GuardRailResult` of violations and warnings.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **SubmissionController / SlotReservationService**

* `POST /submissions/{id}/evaluate-slot`; holds a `held` reservation for Standard drafts (not Fast-Track).

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **FacebookEngagementAnalyticsClient**

* Graph API engagement reads using the active Page token.

* Spring `@Component`

#### ***1.8.4. Object-Oriented Component(s)***

* **Schema**

`CREATE TABLE slot_reservations (`  
    `id         	UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),`  
    `submission_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES submissions(id),`  
	`institution_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES institutions(id),`  
	`scheduled_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,`  
	`status     	VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'held'`  
               	`CHECK (status IN ('held', 'locked', 'released')),`  
	`admin_override BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,  -- set only for an Admin hard-block override`  
	`created_at 	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`  
`);`  
   
`-- GR-H1 enforced by the database (V95/V96): no two active, non-override`  
`-- reservations within ±30 minutes of each other, network-wide.`  
`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION epoch_seconds_immutable(ts timestamptz)`  
`RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE`  
`AS $$ $SELECT(EXTRACT(EPOCHFROMts))::bigint;$ $$;`  
   
`ALTER TABLE slot_reservations ADD CONSTRAINT excl_slot_reservations_network_buffer`  
	`EXCLUDE USING gist (`  
    	`int8range(epoch_seconds_immutable(scheduled_at),`  
                  `epoch_seconds_immutable(scheduled_at) + 1800, '[]') WITH &&`  
	`) WHERE (status <> 'released' AND NOT admin_override);`  
`-- Each reservation covers [t, t + 30 min]; two ranges overlap exactly when the`  
`-- slots are within 30 minutes of each other.`

`Related tables used by this use case:`

`-- page_settings (defined in UC-1.4)`  
`CREATE TABLE page_settings (`  
	`id              	UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),`  
	`institution_id  	UUID REFERENCES institutions(id),`  
	`guardrails_enforced BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,`  
	`posting_window_start_hour INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 8, 	-- GR-H4 window start (Asia/Manila, V116)`  
	`posting_window_end_hour   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 20,	-- GR-H4 window end (exclusive)`  
	`conflict_buffer_minutes   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30,	-- GR-H1 (V121)`  
	`minimum_lead_time_hours   INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 2, 	-- GR-H2 (V121)`  
	`maximum_lead_time_days	INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30,	-- GR-H3 (V121)`  
	`per_institution_active_quota INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,  -- GR-S1 (V122)`  
	`daily_volume_cap      	INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 6, 	-- GR-S2 (V122)`  
`watermark_enabled   BOOLEAN,`  
	`watermark_text  	VARCHAR(150),`  
	`facebook_page_id	VARCHAR(255),`  
	`updated_by      	UUID REFERENCES users(id),`  
	`updated_at      	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`  
`);`

### ***1.9. Draft Submission*** {#1.9.-draft-submission}

#### ***1.9.1. User Interface Design***

**Submit for Approval**

The final action in the composer. The frontend re-checks title, date, caption, media, album, and (Standard) schedule; anything missing jumps back to the relevant step with a toast. If only Recommended items remain, a non-blocking confirmation shows the readiness score ("Submit anyway / Go back").

**Submission Success State**

The composer closes and returns to the Submissions list with the item shown as Pending (or a "Live Event" badge for Fast-Track).

**Slot Conflict at Submit**

On a `409` slot conflict the confirmation closes and the composer returns to Organize & Schedule with a prompt to pick a new time.

**Withdraw Submission**

Available on `pending` items with no review lock; confirmation returns the item to Draft.

#### ***1.9.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**SubmissionScreen (submit flow)**

* `POST /submissions/{id}/submit`; specific `409` handling redirects to the Schedule step.

* React functional component

  **SubmissionListScreen (withdraw)**

* `POST /submissions/{id}/withdraw` with a confirmation prompt.

* React functional component

#### ***1.9.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**SubmissionController**

* `POST /submissions/{id}/submit` (`draft`/`needs_revision`/`rejected` → `pending`), `POST /submissions/{id}/withdraw` (`pending` → `draft`, refused with `409` once a review lock exists).

* Spring `@RestController`

  **SubmissionService**

* `assertContentComplete` (title, date, caption \+ length, media, album) runs before any state change or media reconciliation; Standard drafts are re-validated against the guard rails (`409` on conflict); Fast-Track skips slot validation. On success: reconciles media (new uploads are bound to the institution, filed into the album resolved from `album_name`, marked PROCESSING; library picks keep their album; all receive the post's media tags), clears a prior rejection reason, sets `submitted_at`, and writes `SUBMISSION_SUBMITTED`. Notification failures are caught so they never roll back the transition.

* Spring `@Service`

  **NotificationService**

* T-01 (standard): in-app \+ Messenger to every active Moderator and Administrator. T-11 (Fast-Track): in-app \+ email \+ Messenger, urgent, to every active Moderator and Administrator (`NotificationEventListener.reviewers()`).

* Spring `@Service`

  **SubmissionRepository**

*  `findValidationQueue(priorityCutoff)`, behind GET /validation/queue, orders fast\_track DESC, then submissions due within 30 minutes (GR-T1), then `scheduled_at ASC NULLS LAST`, `submitted_at ASC. findValidationPage`, behind the paginated GET /validation/queue/page that the Review Queue screen uses, orders fast\_track DESC and then the selected sort, without the 30-minute term — there GR-T1 appears only as a badge. SubmissionSummaryDto.priorityFlag marks those due within 30 minutes in both.

* Spring `@Repository`

	`WHERE status IN ('scheduled', 'publishing', 'pending', 'in_review',`

### ***1.10. Moderator Account Management*** {#1.10.-moderator-account-management}

#### ***1.10.1. User Interface Design***

**Moderator Management (User Management, `/admin/user-management`)**

A Moderators card listing network-wide Moderator accounts (no institution) with status badges and pending Moderator invitations. Any active Administrator may Invite, Deactivate, Reactivate, Delete, Resend, and Cancel; Erase is Admin Owner only.

**Change Role Dialog**

Moves an active account between Contributor and Moderator. Contributor → Moderator clears the institution; Moderator → Contributor requires selecting an active institution. Either direction revokes sessions and releases any review locks the account holds.

#### ***1.10.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**UserManagementScreen / InvitationComposer / PendingInvitationsCard / ChangeRoleModal**

* `GET /users/moderators`, `GET /invitations/pending/network`, `POST /invitations` (`role = moderator`), `PATCH /users/{id}/status`, `DELETE /users/{id}`, `POST /users/{id}/erase`, `PATCH /users/{id}/role`, `POST /users/promotion/confirm|decline`, `DELETE /users/{id}/promotion` (one unified promotion flow for both target roles).

* React functional components

#### ***1.10.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**InvitationController / InvitationService** — network-scoped Moderator invitations (no institution), same token, reuse, and conflict rules as UC-1.1.

**UserController / UserService**

* Deactivate/reactivate/delete/erase as in UC-1.1/UC-1.3 (any active Admin; erase Admin Owner only). Role change between Contributor and Moderator: a Contributor → Moderator proposal is stored in the unified `pending_promotion_role/requested_by/expires_at` columns (72 hours) and applied on the target's confirmation; Moderator → Contributor is applied directly. On change: session\_version++, review locks released via ReviewLockService, `MODERATOR_PROMOTION_CONFIRMED` (confirmed proposal) or `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` (direct change) written, affected user notified.

* Spring `@RestController` / `@Service`

  **ReviewLockService** — releases locks held by a deactivated or role-changed Moderator.

## ***2\. Module 2*** {#2.-module-2}

Module 2 delivers the institution-scoped media library (upload, nested albums, AI enrichment, semantic search, lifecycle and deletion), the network-wide Moderator/Administrator approval workflow with failed-publication recovery, and automated brand watermarking at publish time.

### ***2.1. Library Uploads & Albums*** {#2.1.-library-uploads-&-albums}

#### ***2.1.1. User Interface Design***

**Upload Modal (Media Repository)**

Multi-file drag-and-drop accepting JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, MOV, and WebM up to 50 MB each, with per-file progress and inline errors. Before confirming, the actor sets an album (existing, new, nested folder path, or Auto-Match) and at least one tag; a tooltip suggests the event name as a tag. Images show a "Processing…" badge until AI processing finishes; videos are READY immediately.

**Album Auto-Match (library upload)**

Text-based (tag and filename overlap): confident (≥0.6) auto-fills with a reasons badge, ambiguous (≥0.3) lists up to 3 candidates, otherwise manual entry with a notice.

**Album Navigation**

Folder-style nested albums (parent/child) with breadcrumbs, album cards (name, asset count), rename, create, move (re-parent, cycle-guarded), and delete. A shared default-institution library is visible to all Contributors.

**Move to Album**

From the asset menu; an asset always belongs to exactly one album (no "unfiled" option). Cross-institution moves follow role rules.

#### ***2.1.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**MediaRepositoryScreen / MediaToolbar / AlbumCard / AssetCard**

* Grid/list browsing and album navigation; `GET /media-assets/albums`, `POST /media-assets/albums`, `POST /media-assets/albums/{id}` (rename), `POST /media-assets/albums/ensure-path`, `PATCH /media-assets/albums/{id}/parent`, `DELETE /media-assets/albums/{id}`.

* React functional components / Signed-in route

  **UploadModal**

* `POST /media-assets/upload-url` → browser PUT to R2 → `POST /media-assets/upload` with album and tags.

* React modal component

  **AlbumCombobox** — shared with UC-1.7 (`suggestions` prop for ranked candidates).

#### ***2.1.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**MediaAssetController**

* Upload, album, move (`POST /media-assets/{id}/album`), and tag endpoints (`POST /media-assets/{id}/tags`, `DELETE /media-assets/{id}/tags/{tagId}`). `isAuthenticated()` — all three roles.

* Spring `@RestController`

  **MediaAssetService**

* Validates format/size, requires ≥1 manual tag at upload and keeps ≥1 manual tag on removal (AI tags do not count), computes SHA-256 `content_hash`, generates `asset_code`, enforces album rules (no null album, cycle guard), and applies cross-institution move rules (Contributor: own uploads, own institution or shared library; Moderator/Admin: any institution). Queues image processing; videos are marked READY without classification.

* Spring `@Service`

  **MediaStorageService** — R2 presign, upload verification, proxy URL resolution.

  **MediaProcessingQueueService / MediaProcessingWorker**

* DB-backed job queue (media\_processing\_jobs) with leases, retries, max\_attempts, and dead letters. Job types allowed by the database (V117): `RETRIEVAL_EMBEDDINGS, CLASSIFY_AND_EMBED, EMBED_IMAGE_ONLY, BUILD_SUBMISSION_CONTEXT`. Status values: `PENDING, PROCESSING, RETRY, COMPLETED, DEAD` (default 5 attempts, app.media-processing.max-attempts). Administrators list and retry dead letters through MediaProcessingAdminController (`GET/system-health/media-processing/dead-letters, POST /system-health/media-processing/dead-letters/{jobId}/retry, audited MEDIA_PROCESSING_DEAD_LETTER_RETRIED`).

* Spring `@Service` / `@Scheduled` worker

  **AIClassificationService**

* Google Gemini classification (`GeminiVisionClient`, model gemini-3.8-flash by default) into the 14-category taxonomy and an asset type, with description, up to 30 AI tags, and enrichment for scenes, objects, activities, OCR, people-count range, and event hypotheses. For `CLASSIFY_AND_EMBED` jobs it sets `READY` once classification and both Voyage embeddings succeed and `FAILED` otherwise; for `RETRIEVAL_EMBEDDINGS` jobs Gemini enrichment is optional and does not change readiness.

* Spring `@Service`

  **MediaImageEmbeddingService / MediaSemanticEmbeddingService**

* Voyage `voyage-multimodal-3.5` image embeddings and `voyage-4-lite` semantic text embeddings (1024 dimensions) stored in `media_asset_embeddings`

* Spring `@Service`

  **MediaAlbumRepository / AssetTagRepository / MediaAssetRepository**

* Spring `@Repository`. Native queries that hydrate `MediaAsset` list every mapped column explicitly.

	`visible_objects     	TEXT[],`

`);`  
   
`CREATE TABLE media_asset_embeddings (`  
	`id         	UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),`

	`model      	TEXT NOT NULL,`  
	`source_input_hash   	CHAR(64),`  
	`source_revision     	BIGINT,`  
	`processing_version  	VARCHAR(50),`  
	`embedding  	VECTOR(1024) NOT NULL,`  
	`created_at 	TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),`

`CREATE TABLE media_processing_jobs (`  
	`id             	UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),`  
	`asset_id       	UUID REFERENCES media_assets(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
	`submission_id  	UUID REFERENCES submissions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,`  
	`job_type       	VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL`  
                   	`CHECK (job_type IN ('RETRIEVAL_EMBEDDINGS', 'CLASSIFY_AND_EMBED',`  
                                       	`'EMBED_IMAGE_ONLY', 'BUILD_SUBMISSION_CONTEXT')),`  
	`status         	VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL`  
                   	`CHECK (status IN ('PENDING','PROCESSING','RETRY','COMPLETED','DEAD')),`  
	`attempt_count  	INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,`  
	`max_attempts   	INT NOT NULL,`  
	`priority            	SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,`  
	`rerun_requested     	BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,`  
	`next_attempt_at	TIMESTAMPTZ,`  
	`lease_until    	TIMESTAMPTZ,`

### ***2.2. Semantic Search & Filtering*** {#2.2.-semantic-search-&-filtering}

#### ***2.2.1. User Interface Design***

**Media Repository Screen (`/media-repository`)**

A grid/list of assets scoped to the actor's visibility: Contributors see their institution and the shared network-default institution; Moderators and Administrators see the whole network (Network View is always on for them) with an institution filter and institution badges. Each card shows thumbnail or video poster, asset code, editable display title, upload date, size/type, and a Processing badge or AI category. Controls: keyword/semantic search, album filter, institution filter (Moderator/Admin), sort (Newest, Oldest, Name, Size), grid/list toggle, and a result strip with match count and clearable filter chips. An empty state appears when nothing matches.

**Asset Detail Panel**

Media preview (lightbox zoom or video player), read-only asset code, click-to-edit title (Enter/blur saves, Escape cancels), metadata grid (filename, uploader, institution, upload date, album, size, resolution/duration, type), AI Tags with confidence, "Your tags" with add/remove, Used In history (UC-2.3), and actions: Use in New Post, Add to Existing Draft (all roles), Download, Delete.

#### ***2.2.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**MediaRepositoryScreen / useMediaAssets**

* `GET /media-assets` (keyword, album, institution, sort, pagination) and `GET /media-assets/search` (semantic).

* React functional component / hook

  **AssetDetailPanel / AssetLightbox**

* `GET /media-assets/{id}`, `POST /media-assets/{id}/title`, tag endpoints, history (UC-2.3).

* React functional components

  **AddToDraftModal**

* Lists the actor's drafts and attaches via `POST /submissions/{id}/assets`; with no drafts, offers a new post. Reports partial success at the 10-asset limit.

* React modal component

  **MediaLibraryTab (composer and review picker)**

* Library picker with institution filter for Moderator/Admin (defaults to the submission's institution).

* React functional component

#### ***2.2.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**MediaAssetController**

* `GET /media-assets`, `GET /media-assets/search`, `GET /media-assets/{id}`, `POST /media-assets/{id}/title`.

* Spring `@RestController`

  **MediaAssetService**

* Visibility scoping via `TenantScopeService`; keyword matching across filename, display title, asset code, uploader email, AI metadata, and all tags (manual and AI, batch-loaded by `loadAllTagLabels`). A cross-institution request outside visibility returns `404`.

* Spring `@Service`

  **MediaSemanticEmbeddingService / MediaSearchCacheService**

* Voyage query embedding \+ pgvector ranking, with keyword fallback/supplement; short-lived search result caching. Embeddings are not recomputed on tag or title edits.

* Spring `@Service`

### ***2.3. Media History Tracking*** {#2.3.-media-history-tracking}

#### ***2.3.1. User Interface Design***

**Used In Block (Asset Detail Panel)**

Lists submissions referencing the asset (title, date, status badge, jump link subject to access), followed by historical reuse records for deleted submissions shown as "\[Submission Deleted\]". Assets removed from terminal submissions show "\[Asset Deleted\]".

**Activity History**

A per-asset, role-scoped slice of audit events (upload, title/album changes, reuse, deletion).

**Delete Confirmation Modal (tiered)**

* **Blocked** — referenced by a `pending`, `in_review`,`scheduled,`or `publishing` submission; shows the conflicting submissions with links.

* **Warning** — referenced only by `draft`/`needs_revision` submissions; lists affected drafts and requires "Delete Anyway" (`force=true`).

* **Free** — referenced only by terminal submissions or unreferenced; a simple confirmation.

  Bulk delete applies the same tiers per asset.

  **Duplicate Detected**

  On upload, an exact SHA-256 match prompts the actor to use the existing asset or upload anyway.

  **Trash View (Administrator only)**

  Lists soft-deleted assets within the 30-day retention window with Restore, Bulk Restore, Purge, Bulk Purge, and Empty Trash.

#### ***2.3.2. Front-end Component(s)***

**AssetDetailPanel (Used In / history)**

* `GET /media-assets/{id}` (usage) and `GET /media-assets/{id}/history`.

  **DeleteModal**

* `DELETE /media-assets/{id}?force=…`, `POST /media-assets/bulk-delete`.

* React modal component

  **TrashView**

* `GET /media-assets/trash`, `POST /media-assets/trash/{id}/restore`, `POST /media-assets/trash/bulk-restore`, `DELETE /media-assets/trash/{id}`, `POST /media-assets/trash/bulk-purge`, `POST /media-assets/trash/empty`.

* React functional component (Admin)

#### ***2.3.3. Back-end Component(s)***

**MediaAssetController** — history, delete, bulk-delete, and trash endpoints (trash is `hasRole('ADMIN')`).

**MediaAssetService**

* Builds Used In (current relationships \+ historical `MEDIA_ASSET_REUSED` audit rows); tiered deletion authorization (Administrator any asset; Moderator and Contributor only assets they uploaded) and reference tiers; soft delete sets `deleted_at`, `deleted_by_user_id`, status deleted, and removes the asset's embeddings; duplicate detection by `content_hash`.

* Spring `@Service`

  **MediaAssetRetentionService / MediaAssetRetentionPurgeJob**

* After `app.media-assets.deleted-retention-days` (default 30), purges R2 objects and embeddings and marks `purged_at`; restore is possible before purge.

* Spring `@Service` / `@Scheduled`

  **AuditLogService**

* Media lifecycle events (`MEDIA_ASSET_UPLOADED`, `MEDIA_ASSET_REUSED`, album changes, `MEDIA_ASSET_DELETED`, restore/purge).

	`action  	VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,  	-- e.g. MEDIA_ASSET_REUSED, MEDIA_ASSET_DELETED`  
	`ip_address  INET,`  
	`user_agent  TEXT,`  
	`resource_id UUID,                  	-- the media asset (or submission) affected`

`);`
